name: Winnow (E2B, E4B, 12B decision models)

lineage.how_derived: fine-tuned for local typed decisions (yes/no, choice, score) through a /v1/systemone endpoint, ordinary chat remains available

purpose: Local typed decisions, chat and image input from one Gemma 4 fine-tune: the server scores answer options without generating an explanation (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card tag apache-2.0 and LICENSE/NOTICE files present in the repos; the text was not read here.

architecture.kind: Gemma 4 dense (12B) and effective-parameter (E2B, E4B) multimodal models
architecture.drafter: optional MTP assistant GGUF (Gemma-4-12B-IT-Assistant) for chat tokens

variants.notes: NVFP4 8.16, BF16 23.83 GB, mmproj F16 0.18 GB (all in gguf/)

pc-12gb.notes: 12.85 GB against a VRAM budget of 9.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-16gb.variant: Winnow-12B Q8_0, 64K context with an image
pc-16gb.notes: vendor measurement on an RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB: peak device VRAM 15.01 GiB at 65,536 positions with Q8 KV cache (card); not our measurement

pc-24gb.notes: 12.85 GB against a VRAM budget of 21.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-32gb.notes: 12.85 GB against a VRAM budget of 29.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

mac-16-24gb.notes: 12.85 GB against a GPU share of about 12 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-32gb.notes: 12.85 GB against a GPU share of about 22 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-64gb+.notes: 12.85 GB against a GPU share of about 52 GB (KV cache not included)

other: Winnow inference server (github EldanRing/winnow-inference) on llama.cpp-style GGUF
engine_support.notes: Ships GGUFs, but decisions need the project's own server (/v1/systemone); plain llama.cpp serves it only as a chat model.

benchmarks.name: Jev Decision Index 0.3 Vision board Full score
benchmarks.variant: Winnow-12B, rank 6 of 20 as quoted on another model's card

benchmarks.name: Decision Index 0.2.1
benchmarks.variant: Winnow-12B as listed in LiquidAI's table (d1-3B 48.57)

benchmarks.name: generation speed, RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, Q8, short prompt

strengths: A decision model reads a state (text, JSON, images) and a schema of typed questions and returns calibrated probabilities for every option in one forward pass; it does not generate text.
the only decision model with a measured 16 GB card profile (64K context with an image)
NVFP4 cuts memory 13.5 to 9.2 GiB at a 2 to 4 point accuracy cost on Jev and Kev (vendor)
weaknesses: adaptive reasoning did not clearly help (paired change -2.3 to +5.5 points) and raised latency 198 to 743 ms
Q8 and NVFP4 comparisons use previously observed panels
best_for: local routing/judging with a 12B decision model on a 16 GB card

tona_fit.reason: Best fit of the decision models for our hardware (12B Q8 on 16 GB with 64K context), Gemma-4 base, still also a chat model. Same class caveat as the other decision models: a pipeline step, not a worker.
blockers: decision decoding needs the project's server or a Tona implementation of the readout

open_questions: E2B/E4B benchmark numbers (only the 12B card was read in full)
independent evaluation outside the Jev/Kev panels
